What a file opens with when nothing was picked for it or its show; a file without that language keeps its own default.
On: when an episode ends, or reaches its credits mark, the next one starts after a five-second countdown.
Off: playback stops at the end, and the up-next card waits for you to choose.
On: phones on this Wi-Fi find “%1$s” behind their video apps’ Cast button (BubbleUPnP, Bilibili, Tencent Video, iQIYI…) and play on the headset.
Off: the headset does not appear in phones\' cast lists.
On: explosions and music come down and dialogue comes up; a 5.1 track\'s centre channel is lifted too.
Off: the film\'s own dynamics. It can also be switched in the player\'s audio settings.
On: Media3/ExoPlayer — audio track switching, embedded and side-by-side subtitles, more formats.
Off: the system player, as a fallback. Takes effect the next time you open a video.
On: hand it to PICO\'s spatial audio engine. Off: play the film\'s own mix.
On this device, 4K with TrueHD 7.1 drops audio now and then, so it starts off. Takes effect on the next film.
Off: a local HTTP proxy (steady). On: a native file descriptor — lower latency, system player only.
If playback stutters, goes silent or shows black, these two switches are worth trying the other way round.
Deletes every scraped entry and the cover cache, back to the beginning
Your sources stay; scan again and the library rebuilds. Note that entries you fixed by hand survive an ordinary rescan, but emptying is a full reset and takes those with it.
Every scraped entry, the cover cache and the matches you fixed by hand will go. Your sources stay, and scanning again rebuilds it.

Reality NAS Player has no account system, ads or analytics. Your library is stored on the headset. If you enable NAS sync, Reality NAS Player also saves watch progress, favourites and manual matches to the share you choose.

Scanning sends the title read out of a file name — “Interstellar 2014”, say — to public databases such as every.film / NeoDB / Wikidata / OFDb / TMDB, AniList, Bangumi and Jikan, in exchange for a poster and a summary. Never the full path, your server\'s address, your credentials or any device identifier.
A download to the headset is copied from your own server alone; while playing, video travels only between this headset and your own server — no third party in between.
Offline scraping uses local rules for titles and skips online metadata and artwork lookups. You can still play films from your NAS.
What is kept on this headset
The addresses, usernames and passwords for your NAS, WebDAV or Jellyfin live on this headset only, are used to reach your own servers, and are never uploaded.
What was matched, the cover cache, your settings, favourites and history. You can empty them under “Library”.
Reality NAS Player · a spatial poster wall for your library

Reality NAS Player turns the tangle of video files on this headset and your NAS into a poster wall, and plays them in your room by default — the screen pinned to the wall, rather than shutting you into a black box.
This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
AniList · Bangumi · MyAnimeList (Jikan) · OMDb · IMDb Datasets
Anime and rating data come from these community databases; thank you for the open interfaces.
The rooms were created for Reality NAS Player. They use CC0 scans from Poly Haven. The Earth in the space lounge uses the NASA image credited below.
Audio decoding uses FFmpeg\'s libavcodec, libavutil and libswresample (LGPL v2.1+).
FFmpeg is a trademark of the FFmpeg project. Building and replacing it is covered in the notes shipped with the app.

Old formats (RMVB, WMV, FLV, XviD…) play in mpv (LGPL v2.1+) with FFmpeg (LGPL v2.1+), libass (ISC), libplacebo (LGPL v2.1+), HarfBuzz (MIT), FreeType (FreeType License), FriBidi (LGPL v2.1+), Fontconfig (MIT), libunibreak (zlib), libxml2 (MIT) and mpv-android\'s JNI layer (MIT). Building and replacing them is covered in the notes shipped with the app.
